name: Bunbury Airwave

confidence.reason: The structure is clearly visible as a circle on a real near-nadir drone photo of the installed bladder (img1), and a second video frame from a different angle and the design plan graphic agree it is a circle. But no image has a scale bar or geo-reference and no satellite image can show it (it existed about a week in Dec 2019), so the 12 m size comes from news/site text rather than being measured, and the exact location is not traced.
factors: structure clearly visible on a real near-nadir drone photo of the installed bladder, published with RWR's 16 Dec 2019 tear report (taken during the install week; exact day not stated)
outline is an ellipse to within 1.3% (img1) and 3.0% (img4) of radius: a circle seen at ~27 deg and ~48 deg tilt; design graphic img5 also draws a circle

size is calibrated from the text-stated 12 m diameter (ABC, Raised Water Research, Tracks, Bunbury Mail), so the 112 m2 vs 113 m2 agreement is by construction, not an independent check; the circular shape is the only image-derived result, good to about +-7% in axis ratio
no shoreline in img1, so no alongshore/offshore frame, no shoreline angles, and offshore distance comes from text (range 30-50 m across sources, unclear whether to centre or near edge)
no satellite imagery can show it: built and torn in Dec 2019, removed within days; nearest Wayback release at the site holds 2016 imagery; card lat/lon is wrong

main residual ambiguity: the outline includes a paler crescent on the upper-left rim (probably a slumped/damaged quadrant); excluding it would shrink the diameter by about 8% (about 11 m on the same calibration)
verification 2026-10-05: outline-to-edge offset measured on the 29 img1 vertices (mean 3.3 px = 0.13 m, 24 of 29 within 5 px); canonical polygon recomputed independently and reproduced to 0.0005 m

design_version.drawn: The single installed Airwave bladder as it lay on the seabed during the Dec 2019 installation: base about 12 m in diameter, installation about 90% complete when a seam tore (diver spotted the tear on Friday 13 Dec 2019; ABC reported it Monday 16 Dec); removed within about three days. Photo img1 was published on 16 Dec 2019 and probably shows the bladder after or around the tear. The drawing is the PLAN OUTLINE (circular base) only; the as-built profile was not a symmetric hemisphere.
design_version.why_this_one: It is the only full-size version ever installed. Searched 2026-10-05: ABC Listen 2022-10-06 (still working on an improved prototype), Bunbury Mail 2022-03-22 (back in the water targeted for summer 2024), RWR profile page (still 'Planning', 'examining repair options'), Waveco's own site (no Airwave listed). The planned redesign (Tracks, 8 Oct 2021: a stronger compound that can be welded, made in Australia, 'a more classic dome shape to better distribute internal pressure') has only been scale-tested in the Queensland hydraulic test tank, so no later plan outline exists. img5 and img2 are pre-install concept graphics of the same 12 m circular dome, not alternative designs.

scale.evidence: No scale bar, no EXIF, no geo-reference. Ellipse fitted to the traced outline has semi-axes 153.6 px (major) and 137.4 px (minor); the major axis of an obliquely viewed circle is not foreshortened, so major axis 307.1 px = text-stated base diameter 12.0 m (ABC 2019-12-16 '12-metre-wide'; Raised Water Research '12m (40 feet) in diameter on the sea floor'; Tracks 2019 'twelve metres in diameter'; Bunbury Mail 2022 '12 metres wide') -> 25.59 px/m. Camera tilt from nadir ~ acos(137.4/153.6) = 26.5 deg. The scale is therefore text-calibrated, not measured on the photo.

sources.traced_what: outer edge of the pale disc as seen from above (where the pale sand/bladder meets green water), including the paler crescent on the upper-left rim where the dome wall shows; 29 vertices read by eye off an overlay.py zoom grid
sources.match_notes: Outline bbox 306 x 281 px, area 65,673 px2. Ellipse fit RMS deviation only 1.3% of radius (normalised radius 0.967-1.027) -> a circle seen at a mild tilt. After stretching the minor axis by 153.6/137.4 and scaling by 25.59 px/m the outline is 12.07 x 12.09 m, area 112.1 m2 (a perfect 12 m circle = 113.1 m2). Size agreement with the text is by construction (scale from text); the independent information is that the shape is a circle (the ring on the crown is flattened by about the same ratio as the disc, so circle to about +-7% in axis ratio). Verification: brightness-gradient test along the outline normal gave mean |offset| 3.3 px (0.13 m), 24 of 29 vertices within 5 px; 5 vertices (10-13, 18) sit 5-16 px outside the half-brightness edge on a soft fringe (using the half-max edge would shrink the diameter by about 2-3%). The outline deliberately includes the paler crescent on the upper-left rim (separated from the bright dome by a dark band); it also appears on the west side of the disc in img4, so it is not a one-camera artefact, but excluding it would make the disc about 8% narrower (about 11 m). Probably a slumped/damaged quadrant (interpretation only, no source says so about this photo). Overlay: overlays/img1.png (stored and re-rendered versions viewed 2026-10-05).

canonical.frame: metres; origin = centre of the ellipse fitted to the img1 trace; +x along the fitted major axis of the oblique view, +y perpendicular (orientation arbitrary and possibly mirrored). No shoreline is visible in img1, so alongshore/offshore axes and north are undefined; the structure is circular so no reported dimension depends on this.
canonical.derived_from: img1 (trace rectified for the oblique view: minor axis stretched by 153.6/137.4, then scaled by 25.59 px/m, i.e. major axis = 12.0 m text diameter)
canonical.notes: Idealised footprint = circle, D = 12.0 m, area 113.1 m2. Traced polygon (29 vertices) is a slightly inscribed approximation (area 112.1 m2). Built with an explicit rotation/stretch (ellipse centre, rotate to the fitted axes, stretch minor axis by a/b, divide by px/m); geom.py make-canonical was NOT used, so its rotation-sign bug does not affect it. Verification: recomputed independently, all 29 vertices agree to 0.0005 m (axis orientation is arbitrary by construction); vertex 0 (430,194) checked by hand: offset from centre (-16.41,-140.87) px, dot major axis (-0.9144,-0.4047) = 72.0 px = 2.81 m; dot minor axis (-0.4047,0.9144) x 1.1176 = -136.6 px = -5.34 m. distance_offshore_m = 37.5 is the midpoint of the text range 30-50 m (RWR 30-45; Tracks 2019 'approximately 45 metres off the low tide mark'; SurferToday '50 meters from shore'); text only, not measurable from any image, and the sources do not say whether it is to the centre or the near edge.

gemini.summary: Gemini's bunbury shape (reef_footprints.json id 'bunbury') is a regular 24-gon circle R=6.0 m generated by formula, with a made-up local frame; its coordinates (-33.3362, 115.6261) are ~1 km south of the real site, and offshore 38 m and crest 1.8 m are unsourced. Every source it cites is dead, wrong-article or unverifiable (verdicts re-confirmed against the originals 2026-10-05), and none shows a plan outline. Several other Gemini claims are contradicted by fetched sources (see other_claims_checked). It happens to match the true plan shape (a 12 m circle) because 12 m is stated everywhere; nothing from it was used here.
